fields.h1: Build a Fantasy Football Sign-Up Sheet for the Whole Preseason
fields.hero_description: Build a fantasy football sign up sheet that caps your league at a set number of teams and polls managers on draft night.
fields.features_heading: What the Commissioner Needs Before Draft Night
fields.features_subheading: A fantasy football sign up sheet records who is in. Emergent builds one that also keeps a waitlist and runs the draft-night poll.
fields.feature_1:
A team cap with a waitlist behind it

Set the league at 10, 12, or 14 teams. The sheet closes at that number, and each later sign-up joins a waitlist in the order it arrived, ready for the first manager who drops.
fields.feature_2:
The email the league invite goes to

Ask each manager for a team name and the email address the league app will invite. A typo caught on the sheet beats resending invites the week of the draft, when nobody reads email.
fields.feature_3:
Keeper picks held to your league's limit

Returning managers name their keepers and the round each one costs. The form accepts no more than the limit you set, so a third keeper in a two-keeper league never reaches the list.
fields.feature_4:
A draft-night poll with a running count

List the nights and times you can host the draft, and each manager marks every one that works. The dashboard counts yes votes per night, so the commissioner picks with numbers.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders for managers who go quiet

Set a deadline for sign-ups or keepers. Anyone who has not answered two days before it gets an email reminder, and the commissioner sees the names still missing on one screen.
fields.feature_6:
Your league's code, on your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host the sheet wherever you like. Next season, change it with a new prompt or edit the code yourself.

fields.tab_content_1:
Into the waitlist goes team 13

Dunhollow Logistics fills its office league at 12 teams, the cap commissioner Mireya Gunnarsen set on the sheet. A dispatcher signs up thirteenth with a team called Pallet Jacks and goes first on the waitlist. Mireya sees all 13 sign-ups on her dashboard. If a manager drops before the draft, Pallet Jacks gets the seat.
fields.tab_content_2:
Keeper picks from all but one manager

Keepers come due 7 days before the draft in the Tullamore Road keeper league, where 10 managers return. Each one names up to 2 players to keep. Nine lists are in 2 days before the deadline. Desh Kavanagh gets an email reminder, and his team shows on the commissioner's missing list.
fields.tab_content_3:
Draft on Thursday at 8 pm, which suits 11 of 14

The Amberleigh Taproom league has 14 managers, and organizer Renzo Haskard put three draft nights on the sign-up sheet. Each manager checks every night that works. Thursday at 8 pm gets 11 yes votes, Friday at 7 pm gets 8 and Sunday at 1 pm gets 6. Renzo emails the league that the draft is Thursday at 8 pm.
fields.tab_content_4:
By 5 votes to 3, the family picks PPR

The family league has 8 Brumfields, and its sheet asks each one to vote on scoring. A PPR league gives a player a point for every catch, and a standard league gives none. PPR wins 5 votes to 3. Commissioner Bea Brumfield sees the count on her dashboard and sets the league to PPR before the invites go out.

fields.howto_title: Making a Fantasy Football Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Plan a fantasy football sign up sheet in seven steps that fill the league and settle the draft date, then build it in Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the email the invite goes to
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Offer two or three draft nights
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle the league size before anyone signs up. The draft order, the weekly schedule, and the playoff bracket all hang on that number. Set it as the cap on the sheet and let later sign-ups fall onto a waitlist.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the email address each manager uses with the league app, not only a name. The commissioner sends invites to those addresses, and one wrong letter leaves a manager outside the league on draft night.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Show the keeper questions only to people who played last season. Set the most players each can keep and ask which draft round each keeper uses up. Put the deadline a week before the draft.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the nights and start times you can host, and let managers check every one they can make. A yes or no for each night gives a cleaner count than asking for a single favorite.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put scoring to a vote if it is open
fields.howto_step_5_des: If the league has not settled scoring, add a vote between PPR and standard. Close the vote before the invites go out. Every manager then drafts under one set of rules from the first pick of the night.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with two made-up managers
fields.howto_step_6_des: Fill in the sheet twice yourself, once as a new manager and once as a returning one with keepers. Check that both rows land in the database with the right team names and that the keeper limit holds.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Write the league out in plain English, starting with its team cap, keeper limit, draft nights, and scoring vote. Emergent builds the sheet and its database. Change it by prompt when a manager asks for something new.

faq_plan.q: What is a fantasy football sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: A fantasy football sign up sheet is the form a commissioner sends before the season to collect each manager's name, team name, and contact email for the league invite. A league can put keeper picks, draft-night availability, and a scoring vote on the same sheet.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a fantasy football sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI form builder about the league in plain English: the team cap, what each manager answers, and any keeper or draft-night section. Emergent builds the sheet and a database for the answers. Run two test entries, then share the link with the league.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a fantasy football sign up sheet ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the manager's name, a team name, and an email address for the league app's invite. Add a phone number if the league talks by text. Returning leagues add keepers, and new leagues add a draft-night poll. Keep the first page to those basics so nobody quits halfway.

faq_plan.q: How do I cap the number of managers on a fantasy football sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Put a team cap on the sign-up sheet. Once the cap is reached, the sheet stops seating new managers and lists each later sign-up on a waitlist by arrival time. When a seated manager drops out, offer the seat to the first name on that list.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect keeper picks on a fantasy football sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Add a keeper section that only returning managers fill in, with a limit on how many players each can name. Ask for the player's name and position for each keeper. Set the due date a week before the draft to leave time to sort out disputes.

faq_plan.q: Can a fantasy football sign up sheet poll managers on a draft night?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each night its own question with the start time attached, and let managers answer all of them. Count the yes votes per night and pick the highest. Announce the winner to the whole league by email, and put the date on the sheet's confirmation page for late joiners.

faq_plan.q: Should a fantasy football sign up sheet include a scoring vote?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when scoring is still open. ESPN's help center says that in a PPR league, players who catch a reception earn a point, while standard leagues do not award a point for a catch. Close the vote before the draft.

faq_plan.q: How do I send reminders from a fantasy football sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Set a sign-up deadline and send an email reminder two days before it to anyone on last season's list who has not answered. The app Emergent builds can send that email on a schedule and show the commissioner who is still missing.

faq_plan.q: Where do fantasy football sign up sheet answers get stored?
faq_plan.a: Every answer lands as a row in one table: one row per manager, with team name, email, keepers, and draft-night votes. With Emergent, that table sits in a database you own, and no response caps cut off a big league partway through sign-ups.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse a fantasy football sign up sheet next season?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep last season's managers in the table and send them the same link with this year's dates. Change the questions by prompt when the league adds a keeper or switches scoring. On paid plans, the full code can be exported to your GitHub repository.

plan.angle: The top 10 for fantasy football sign up sheet is template pages (survey and form builders, printable sheets on Pinterest) and the big platforms' league-creation screens. Those collect a name and a team name. This page shows the sheet as the commissioner's preseason desk: a team cap with a waitlist for an office league, keeper picks collected before a deadline, a draft-night poll that settles the date, and a scoring vote that sets PPR or standard before anyone opens the league app. The how-to and FAQ cover what templates skip: league size, the invite email field, deadlines tied to draft night, and keeping the sheet's answers in one table.
